info.title: Auth Public OpenAPI v1
info.description: Public surface for trusted company backends. Each application is one machine principal with its own client credentials, its own scopes and its own directory range. HTTPS is required, the application egress IP allowlist is enforced, employee access uses browser authorization with mandatory S256 PKCE or the registered enterprise mini-program extension grant, and machine access uses the client-credentials grant. Access tokens last up to 24 hours, are opaque and are re-checked against the database on every call. See docs/openapi.md for deployment and rollout.

get.summary: Browser login and authorization code with mandatory S256 PKCE
get.description: Redirects the browser to the registered callback with `code` and the echoed `state`. The caller opens this endpoint in a browser; the application backend never calls it. A login that no longer passes the configured admission rule is answered with `login_required`. `prompt=login`, `max_age=0`, or an interactive request whose login exceeds `max_age` sends the browser through the platform login first. All authorization parameters are preserved; a one-time completion bound to the exact request and new session proves the login. With `prompt=none`, an absent or insufficiently fresh browser session returns `error=login_required` and the original `state` to the validated registered callback without opening a login page.

400.description: Invalid request, scope, grant or body

401.description: Invalid client or token, or a login that no longer passes admission; WWW-Authenticate is included

403.description: HTTPS, application IP, scope or directory range refused access

404.description: The named object is outside this application or does not exist

409.description: The object already exists, is still referenced, or the settings revision is stale

302.description: Redirect to the registered callback URI with code/state, or error=login_required/state when a silent request has no valid browser session

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Space-separated subset of the registered user scopes

parameters.name: max_age
parameters.description: OIDC `max_age`: only accept a browser login that happened at most this many seconds ago. A login older than the window, or whose instant is unknown, requires a new platform login; with `prompt=none` it returns `login_required` to the validated callback instead. 0 requires a one-time proof of login for this exact request and session; the maximum is 30 days.

parameters.name: nonce
parameters.description: OIDC `nonce`, echoed into the ID Token when `openid` is among the scopes. It is stored with the authorization code, because the token endpoint runs without a browser session; a nonce longer than 128 characters or carrying a line break is rejected as `invalid_request`.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: OIDC `prompt`. `login` forces a fresh interactive authentication: the browser is sent to the platform login and returns to this same request without the parameter. With `none`, an absent or expired browser session returns `error=login_required` and the original `state` to the validated registered callback without entering the login flow. Invalid requests and unregistered callback addresses never redirect. Any other value is rejected as `invalid_request` — this deployment shows neither consent nor account selection.

post.summary: Start authorization with a form POST
post.description: Converts a bounded form to the same-origin GET authorization endpoint with 303. No grant is issued by POST; the GET enforces browser authentication, exact callbacks, login admission, fresh-login requirements and S256 PKCE. Query parameters and duplicate form fields are refused.

303.description: Continue on the same-origin GET authorization endpoint

400.description: Invalid form

403.description: HTTPS required

post.summary: Exchange a browser authorization code, enterprise mini-program code or machine credential for an access token
post.description: `authorization_code` redeems a code for an opaque employee access token valid for up to 86400 seconds; its scopes come from the code, never from this request. `client_credentials` mints a machine token whose scopes are the requested subset of the registered machine scopes, valid for 86400 seconds. `urn:waywake:params:oauth:grant-type:wecom-mini-program` exchanges a wx.qy.login code through the calling application's registered mini_program_appid/credential_ref binding for the same employee identity and IAM permissions as browser login. Client, grant, scope and binding checks precede the upstream exchange; openid is refused and no ID Token is issued. Use /me for identity. Client credentials and Auth tokens stay in the business backend. Normal browser and mini-program logins coexist. A successfully exchanged upstream code cannot be restored after a database failure; obtain a new wx.qy.login code. `refresh_token` is served once continuous authorization is configured; refresh tokens expire at the session's fixed absolute deadline, up to 72 hours after initial authorization. Rotation uses the remaining session lifetime and never extends that deadline. Previously issued refresh tokens keep their stored expiry; a still-valid token's replacement uses the remaining session lifetime. Access expires_in is shortened near the deadline. Form-encoded body only. Authenticate with exactly one of client_secret_basic or client_secret_post. The empty security alternative represents required client_id and client_secret form fields, not anonymous access. Duplicate credentials or combining header and body authentication returns invalid_request. Credentials in query strings are refused.

post.summary: Revoke one credential issued to this application
post.description: Unknown credentials, credentials of another application and already-revoked credentials all answer 200 with an empty body, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe for live tokens. Revoking a refresh token atomically ends its authorization session, the entire refresh family and the employee's access tokens in that application. Authenticate with exactly one of client_secret_basic or client_secret_post. The empty security alternative represents required client_id and client_secret form fields, not anonymous access. Duplicate credentials or combining header and body authentication returns invalid_request. Credentials in query strings are refused.

get.summary: Read the JSON Web Key Set that verifies ID Tokens
get.description: The public halves of the deployment's ID Token signing keys, in rotation order: the first key signs, every published key still verifies. A client that was issued an `id_token` fetches this document and verifies the RS256 signature against the key named by the token's `kid` header. An installation with no signing keyring answers 503 instead of an empty key list, because a client would cache an empty list as "this issuer has no keys".

503.description: This installation has no signing keyring, so it issues no ID Tokens

get.summary: End the browser session a relying party asks to close
get.description: RP-Initiated Logout. The relying party redirects the browser here with the ID Token it was issued and its current authenticated browser cookie. The hint's signature, issuer and audience are verified, and its sub and signed sid must match that exact browser session, including same-second re-logins. Expired hints remain usable when they match; hints without sid or from another session are rejected without revoking a session or clearing a cookie. Legacy sid-less hints require a fresh authorization. HEAD is refused. The browser session version advances and logout notifications for its recorded OIDC relying parties are persisted in the same transaction, including clients without refresh tokens. Back-channel delivery carries the original signed sid so a delayed notification cannot end a newer login. The browser cookie is cleared only after this transaction succeeds. If `post_logout_redirect_uri` names a target registered for that application the browser is sent there with `state` echoed; otherwise the deployment's own login page is the landing. An unregistered target is refused with `invalid_request` — after the session has ended, because the logout is the point of the request.

get.summary: Read the OIDC discovery document
get.description: The standard discovery document: the issuer identity, the endpoint URLs, the supported response type, grant types, PKCE method, scopes and the ID Token signing algorithm. Every URL is built from the public Base URL the deployment is configured with, which is the same value an ID Token states as `iss`. An installation with no signing keyring answers 503, because its issuer could not mint the tokens a client would configure itself to request.

get.summary: Read the OIDC discovery document
get.description: OIDC discovery at the issuer's standard well-known location. The issuer is the public Base URL, matching the metadata and ID Token iss. The original /openapi/v1/.well-known/openid-configuration URL remains an equivalent alias. An installation with no signing keyring answers 503.

get.summary: Read the subject the presented access token stands for
get.description: The standard OIDC userinfo answer, served as a bare object rather than inside the API's `data` envelope. `sub` is the same decimal employee identifier the ID Token states, so a client can tie the two together. `name`, `preferred_username` and `picture` are included only when the token also carries `profile` or legacy `profile:read`. `email` and `email_verified` require the separate `email` scope; verification is false because the directory contains no verification evidence. `openid` names a subject, it does not widen what the application may read about the employee. A token without `openid` is answered with `insufficient_scope`.

get.summary: Read an employee's leave records and balances inside the current directory range
get.description: Requires a client-credentials machine token carrying the operation's machine scope. A machine token never carries an employee identity, never has a refresh counterpart, and is refused on every employee resource. Requires the independent leave:read scope; directory:read does not authorize leave data. The current directory range is rechecked on every request. Hidden and departed employees answer 404. An unconfigured leave source answers 503; an employee not yet synchronized has synced_at and on_leave set to null. No leave reason or attachment is exposed. Balances preserve the upstream day/hour unit: a day is 86400 seconds, an hour is 3600 seconds. Consumers must inspect synced_at before treating the snapshot as current.

client_id.description: Required with client_secret_post; omit with HTTP Basic

client_secret.description: Required with client_secret_post; omit with HTTP Basic

LogoutRedirect.description: This operation answers a 302 redirect, not a JSON body

issuer.description: Public Base URL, identical to the `iss` claim of an ID Token

sub.description: Employee identifier, equal to the `sub` of the ID Token

email.description: Only with `email`; omitted when no address is recorded

email_verified.description: Returned with email; the directory provides no independent verification evidence

JsonWebKeySet.description: Only public parameters are published: the private exponent and the primes never leave the deployment.

kid.description: Key identifier, equal to the `kid` header of the tokens this key signed

access_token.description: Opaque `oat_` employee token or `oam_` machine token

expires_in.description: Actual remaining access-token lifetime in seconds; up to 24 hours, shortened near the authorization session's absolute deadline

refresh_token.description: Present only for a refreshable employee grant

id_token.description: Signed RS256 ID Token, present exactly when the authorization asked for `openid`. The keys to verify it are published at `/openapi/v1/.well-known/jwks.json`. An installation with no signing keyring refuses `openid` at the authorize endpoint, so this field is never silently absent for a client that requested it.

client_id.description: Required with client_secret_post; omit with HTTP Basic

client_secret.description: Required with client_secret_post; omit with HTTP Basic

client_id.description: Required with client_secret_post; omit with HTTP Basic

client_secret.description: Required with client_secret_post; omit with HTTP Basic

exp.description: Unix expiry, present only when active

next_change_at.description: The next scheduled authorization transition, when one exists

credential_id.description: The client credential that bootstrapped this token

status.description: WeCom approval status; only 2 (approved) contributes to on_leave

remaining_seconds.description: Upstream remaining quota, including a negative value when permitted by the supplier policy

on_leave.description: Approved interval covers the current time; null before the first successful synchronization

next.description: 0 on the last page, otherwise the cursor to pass as `after`

provider.description: Trimmed and uppercased provider code; 1 to 32 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens

tenant_id.description: Trimmed, case-sensitive opaque tenant ID, at most 128 UTF-8 bytes; control characters are refused

namespace.description: Trimmed and uppercased identity namespace; 1 to 32 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens

external_id.description: Trimmed, case-sensitive opaque account ID, at most 128 UTF-8 bytes; control characters are refused

parent_id.description: 0 when the parent is outside the configured range

expires_at.description: Omit for a permanent grant; a past instant is rejected

overlap_seconds.description: How long a replaced key keeps authenticating

revision.description: Optimistic lock; submit the value you read

revocation_version.description: Authorization epoch; advances only for a security-policy change

grant_types.description: refresh_token requires authorization_code or the enterprise mini-program grant; only authorization_code requires redirect_uris

mini_programs.description: Fixed mini-program bindings; required when enabling the mini-program grant. Changes advance revocation_version.

connect_hosts.description: The legacy browser login hand-off's own allowlist, independent of the machine configuration

connect_verified.description: Whether an administrator has confirmed the legacy list

credentials_present.description: Whether any unrevoked client credential exists

store_scope.description: Independent brand/store union. Empty denies all stores. Brand access includes future stores. Changes revoke existing tokens.
Independent brand/store union. Empty denies all stores. Brand access includes future stores. Changes revoke existing tokens.

credential_ref.description: Deployment credential name, bound to the same mini-program AppID; no upstream secret is returned or accepted in settings

secret.description: Shown exactly once; never persisted or logged

id.description: Stable event identifier; the same value is redelivered and is what a receiver deduplicates on

sequence.description: This application's own dense cursor, assigned at publish time

subject_id.description: Stable identifier within the subject kind. For browser_session, this is the application's smallest exchanged OIDC grant ID for the ended browser login; payload.browser_session_id carries the original ID Token sid.

expires_at.description: Retention deadline; once the cursor is older than this the pull answers 410

data.description: Event-specific payload; the fields are additive within a type

has_more.description: The unfiltered scan page filled up; follow next immediately even when the type filter returned no events

id.description: Audit row identifier; the page cursor is built from it

actor_id.description: Employee actor, 0 when a machine acted

actor_app_id.description: Application that acted, 0 when a person acted

app_id.description: Application the row concerns, 0 when the row names none

status.description: HTTP status the recorded request answered

next.description: Pass as `before` to read the next page; 0 means the history ends here

from.description: Inclusive first day of the window, at local midnight

calls.description: Recorded rows over the whole window

day.description: Calendar day the rows were recorded on

latency.description: How long the window's measured calls took. `measured` counts the calls that carried a duration at all, so the difference from `calls` is the audit rows that describe work which was not a served request (a scheduled job or a background worker) plus rows written before durations were recorded. The buckets are cumulative: a call within `upper_ms` also appears in every larger bucket.

measured.description: Calls of this window that carried a duration

average_ms.description: Mean duration over the measured calls of the whole window, truncated to milliseconds; 0 when nothing was measured

maximum_ms.description: Slowest measured call of the window

p95_upper_ms.description: Smallest published bound whose cumulative count covers 95% of the measured calls — an upper bound read off the buckets, not an exact quantile. 0 when nothing was measured or when even the largest bound does not cover 95%.

upper_ms.description: The published bound; the set is fixed so two reports are comparable

calls.description: Measured calls at or under this bound, over the whole window

rate_limit.description: How much of its own per-minute budgets the application has already spent in the current window. Null when the counter store could not be read; the report never fabricates zeros.

purpose.description: token: the application-wide budget, machine: the machine-token budget, resource: the employee-resource budget. The peer budget is keyed by client address and the authorize budget by employee, so neither is attributable to the application

used.description: Requests already spent in the current window; observing it spends nothing

resets_in_seconds.description: How long until the current window is refunded, rounded up; 0 means nothing is currently spent. A caller refused with 429 can wait this long instead of guessing.

kind.description: `event`: the signed JSON change event, verified with the endpoint's own signing key. `logout`: an OIDC back-channel logout endpoint, which receives a `logout_token` form post instead — the URL is the relying party's back-channel logout URI, and the registration is refused while this deployment holds no ID Token keyring. A logout subscription must name `session.revoked` as its only event type.

last_status.description: HTTP status of the last attempt, 0 when none completed

last_error.description: Redacted failure of the last attempt

live.description: Not revoked and not past its absolute deadline

absolute_expires_at.description: Fixed when the employee approved; never extended by a refresh

event_types.description: The closed vocabulary a subscription may name

secret.description: Shown exactly once; the receiver verifies delivery signatures with it

backlog.description: Deliveries still waiting to be attempted

url.description: Public HTTPS endpoint; a rotation, a pause and a delete identify the endpoint by `subscription_id` instead and may omit it

event_types.description: Omitted `kind` (or `kind: event`) accepts any of the change events; `kind: logout` accepts exactly `session.revoked`

kind.description: Payload shape this endpoint receives; omitted means `event`, which is what every registration before back-channel logout was

subscription_id.description: Set by the state, rotation and delete routes

certificates.description: Public RSA signing certificates in PEM; private keys are forbidden

delivery_time_requirement.description: 可选送货时间要求，未填写为空字符串

next.description: Opaque cursor bound to application, filter and policy epoch; empty at end

primary_store.description: Null means no visible primary; it does not disclose whether a hidden primary exists

x-error-codes.invalid_client: Unknown application, wrong credential, disabled integration or credential outside the allowlist
x-error-codes.invalid_grant: Code, verifier, redirect or refresh token refused
x-error-codes.invalid_scope: Requested scope outside the registered vocabulary
x-error-codes.invalid_token: Bearer credential unknown, expired, revoked or of the wrong kind
x-error-codes.insufficient_scope: The credential does not carry the scope the operation requires
x-error-codes.login_required: The employee must sign in again, or no longer passes the configured admission rule
x-error-codes.unsupported_grant_type: The application is not configured for the requested grant
x-error-codes.https_required: The request did not provably arrive over HTTPS
x-error-codes.ip_not_allowed: The calling peer is outside the application's egress allowlist
x-error-codes.not_found: The named object is outside this application or does not exist
x-error-codes.conflict: The settings revision is stale, or the object still has references
x-error-codes.rate_limit_exceeded: The per-minute budget for this key is exhausted; retry after 60 seconds
x-error-codes.temporarily_unavailable: A dependency is unavailable; access is refused rather than degraded
